question: During a New-Year sale, a company gives a ‘Buy 9 Sweaters and Get 1 Free’ offer to customers. The percentage discount involved in this deal is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In 'Buy X Get Y Free' offers, the discount is calculated on the total number of items.

Total Items = Paid Items + Free Items = 9 + 1 = 10

Discount % = (Free Items ÷ Total Items) × 100

Discount % = (1 ÷ 10) × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Buy = 9 sweaters, Free = 1 sweater.

Formula: Discount % = [Free Items ÷ (Buy Items + Free Items)] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b62d4a16409d2d9cfbdfb6c628c11b58ac9bea12370ff2ba692bfd6343ce7c28.png] 

Let the Marked Price (MP) of each sweater be ₹1.

⇒ Total MP for 10 sweaters = 10 × 1 = ₹10

⇒ Customer pays for only 9 sweaters.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) for 10 sweaters = 9 × 1 = ₹9

⇒ Discount Amount = MP − SP = 10 − 9 = ₹1

⇒ Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 10) × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two discounts d₁ and d₂ are applied, effective discount = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100.

Markup Percentage

Markup % is the percentage by which MP is higher than CP: [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Profit and Discount Relationship

The ratio of MP to CP is given by: MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).
